decision: NARROWED BEYOND LANGUAGE-INTERNAL TOPIC IDENTIFIABILITY — RQ-001 NOT ADOPTED
finding: Anchor-word, anchor-free, and testable-separability results can identify or audit a raw-language latent decomposition under explicit assumptions, but they do not identify the external target quotient P or the relative denotation alignment d. A language anchor fixes a language-simplex vertex, not a world target. Language dynamics may shrink the joint identified set only through an explicit cross-system observation or linking assumption.
prior_art: Arora et al. 2013 separable anchor-word topic recovery
Freyaldenhoven et al. 2025 testability of anchor-word separability
Lee et al. 2019 Rectified Anchor Word practical implementation materials
counterexamples: perfectly identified language topics and target blocks retain an unconstrained relative permutation
two separable discourse/register topics may denote one physical target
one language topic may denote multiple context-conditioned targets
passing a separability test does not validate external grounding
rq_remaining: After separately identifying or partially identifying Q and the exact full-consequence controlled P, determine which preregistered joint observation laws identify relative alignment or context-indexed denotation, while excluding language-internal anchors, cardinality assumptions, and semantic leakage.
